implementation_notes: Node's stdlib already separates establishment from processing: server.listen() binds and accepts (acceptor), the 'connection' event hands a net.Socket to a per-connection handler, and net.createConnection()/net.connect() is the connector ('connect' event on the returned socket). http.Server and tls.Server compose the same split one layer up.
pitfalls: Blocking the event loop inside a connection handler stalls every connection; delegate to a worker thread or use stream.pipe() for back-pressure.
An unhandled 'error' event on a socket or server terminates the process; always attach an error handler.
The listen backlog is only a soft bound; enforce admission control in user space.
Destroying a socket mid-write corrupts data; drain writes before close.
Server.listen() may bind to a random port if 0 is passed; read server.address() to discover the actual port in tests.
